title: Persatrix Channel Configuration (v0.3.0+)
description: Internal-only schema until v1.0; `$id` may break across v0.x bumps without notice. Per RFC 0011 §A the canonical channel address is derived at runtime as `<channel_type>:<name>` (e.g., `group:planning`); the SQL `channels.id` PK column is a separate concern. DMs open on demand and are not declared here; threads anchor to a parent message and are likewise implicit.

max_channels.description: Global cap on declared named group channels. DMs and threads are not counted.

max_cascade_depth.description: Primary-enforcement cap on the cooperative-path cascade-depth backstop (RFC 0011 amendment 'Cascade-depth wire propagation', PR 2). Default is 5, aligned with the Python dispatcher's `max_cascade_depth` (agents/dispatch.py). The Go loader treats a zero or absent value as 'use the orchestrator default' so the backstop cannot be silently disabled from config (ChannelRouter.SetMaxCascadeDepth ignores non-positive overrides). Negative values are not permitted by the schema so an operator typo surfaces at `make validate` time rather than as a silent fall-back at startup.

default_interaction_budget_tokens.description: RFC 0030 Layer 1 (v0.3.8) fleet-wide per-interaction cost ceiling in tokens, applied to any channel that omits its own `interaction_budget_tokens`. Opt-in: 0 (the default) means uncapped, so the ceiling is additive and existing channels are unchanged. Once an interaction's running token total would cross the resolved ceiling, the wallet denies further leases in that interaction (`INTERACTION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, fail-closed — the LLM call does not happen). Negative is rejected at load time.

default_max_replies_per_participant.description: RFC 0030 Layer 2 (v0.3.8) fleet-wide per-participant reply budget, applied to any channel that omits its own `max_replies_per_participant_per_interaction`. Opt-in: 0 (the default) means uncapped, so fair-turn-taking is additive and existing channels are unchanged. With K>0, a participant's (K+1)th publish in one interaction is rejected pre-persistence (HTTP 429); a human principal listed in `governance.exempt_principals` is exempt. Negative is rejected at load time.

default_interaction_idle_timeout_seconds.description: Fleet-wide interaction idle window in seconds (the RFC 0030 interaction-id producer, IP3), applied to any channel that omits its own `interaction_idle_timeout_seconds`: a publish arriving more than this long after the channel's last one retires the open interaction and mints a fresh one (`interaction_closed{trigger=idle}`). Absent means 600 — RFC 0020 §B's idle default, matching the agent-side `interaction_idle_timeout_sec` so governance and memory boundaries roughly coincide. An explicit 0 disables idle rotation fleet-wide (distinct from absent). Thread channels ignore the resolved value entirely — a thread IS its interaction. Negative is rejected at load time.

dm_default_classification.description: RFC 0037 §B (v0.3.12) fleet-wide confidentiality classification stamped onto DM channels at creation. DMs open on demand (`dm:<a>:<b>`) with no per-channel config block, so this knob is their only declaration point; an existing DM keeps its creation-time stamp (the config-reconcile reclassification path covers declared group channels only). Absent means `internal` — §A rule (a): a conversation surface nobody classified is confidential-by-default, never `public`. All four levels are honoured since the §D gate armed (RFC 0037 PR 4 deleted the item-8 dark-window ceiling that rejected `restricted`/`secret` at startup) — operators running sensitive DMs can raise this.

governance.description: RFC 0030 (v0.3.8) fleet-wide governance settings that are not per-channel.

exempt_principals.description: Principal classes exempt from the Layer 2 per-participant reply budget (§OQ-7). The only recognised value is `human`, which maps to the `user` participant type on the wire so a human driving a conversation is never throttled by the budget meant to keep agents from dominating. An entry with no mapping is ignored (fails open to 'not exempt').

classification.description: RFC 0037 §A (v0.3.12) confidentiality classification for this group channel — the fixed four-level lattice (`public` < `internal` < `restricted` < `secret`) the memory confidentiality boundary compares against. Absent means `internal` (§A rule (a): confidential-by-default, never `public`). LOAD-BEARING since RFC 0037 Phases 1–3 shipped (v0.3.12): the level is stamped on the store row, lifted onto every `ChannelMessageEvent`, and read by the §D memory-injection egress gate and §F recall filter; reclassify by changing the declared value and re-applying config (the reconcile path adopts it, no restart). The item-8 dark-window ceiling that rejected a declared `restricted`/`secret` at startup was deleted when the §D gate armed (PR 4) — all four levels are enforceable boundaries. Operator surface: the channels guide's classification section.

revision.description: RFC 0050 Phase 1 per-channel config revision (the revision-gated loader). The monotonic, store-owned version this YAML block was exported at. At boot the loader writes the block into the canonical channel store ONLY if its revision is strictly greater than the store's current revision for that channel; equal revision with differing content is surfaced as drift (the store stays authoritative — `channel config diff` inspects it) and an older revision is ignored, so the higher revision always wins. Absent or 0 is seed-only: it never overrides a store edit (a channel the store has had edited sits at revision > 0), so existing hand-authored configs are left untouched. `channel config export` stamps `store + 1` automatically; to roll back, write the old config as a NEW higher revision — never decrement. Negative is rejected at load time.

floor_control.description: RFC 0030 Layer 2.5 speaker serialization (floor control): candidate responders take the floor one at a time, each reading the prior speaker's reply, instead of replying concurrently and mutually-blind. As of v0.3.6 the resolved default is ON for every declared (group) channel — omit the key to inherit it; set it false to opt a channel back out. Below two responders (e.g. a DM) it is a no-op regardless. The per-turn wait is floor_turn_timeout_seconds.

floor_turn_timeout_seconds.description: Per-speaker turn timeout for floor control (RFC 0030 amendment decision D2): how long the serialized loop waits for one speaker's reply before advancing to the next responder. Distinct from the 5s per-recipient fanout timeout — a floor turn is LLM-latency-bound. Absent uses the 45s default; the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time.

salience_max_channel_members.description: RFC 0030 Tier B (v0.3.8) channel-size cap (TB6 / amendment OQ #4): above this many candidate responders, the agent-side salience bid is skipped entirely and open-floor `participant`/`chair` members fall back to `addressed`-only, keeping a cheap bid × N members bounded on a large channel. Absent uses the 20 default (kept in lock-step with the agent-side DEFAULT_SALIENCE_MAX_CHANNEL_MEMBERS); the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time. The resolved value is carried to the agent on the ChannelMessageEvent wire.

max_cascade_depth.description: ISSUE-0114 (v0.3.13) per-channel RFC 0030 Layer 0 cascade-depth cap — post-ISSUE-0109 the de facto length knob for a productive autonomous discussion (the continuation advances round tally and reply depth together, so this cap binds before max_rounds on every productive chain). Opt-in: absent or 0 inherits the top-level `max_cascade_depth` (itself 0 = the orchestrator default 5); like the fleet knob, 0 can never disable the cap. Negative is rejected here and at load time. The Go loader ALSO rejects a value above the resolved fleet cap — a cross-field rule this schema cannot express (ISSUE-0114 option (c)): the Python dispatcher's defense-in-depth cap is a per-process global aligned by convention with the fleet value, so a per-channel cap above it would be silently unreachable. Raising one channel past the fleet default means raising the fleet cap (and the aligned agents/dispatch.py backstop) first.

interaction_budget_tokens.description: RFC 0030 Layer 1 (v0.3.8) per-interaction cost ceiling in tokens for this channel. Once an interaction on this channel would cross the ceiling, the wallet denies further leases (`INTERACTION_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, fail-closed). Opt-in: absent or 0 inherits `default_interaction_budget_tokens` (itself 0 = uncapped) — unlike `salience_max_channel_members`, 0 is NOT normalized to a non-zero default, because uncapped is a meaningful value. Negative is rejected at load time. The channel-over-fleet precedence is resolved at read time.

max_replies_per_participant_per_interact.description: RFC 0030 Layer 2 (v0.3.8) per-participant reply budget for this channel: a participant's (K+1)th publish in one interaction on this channel is rejected pre-persistence (HTTP 429 + `ErrParticipantBudgetExhausted`), so the dropped message never enters channel history. Opt-in: absent or 0 inherits `default_max_replies_per_participant` (itself 0 = uncapped) — like `interaction_budget_tokens`, 0 is NOT normalized to a non-zero default, because uncapped is a meaningful value. A human principal in `governance.exempt_principals` is exempt. Negative is rejected at load time. The channel-over-fleet precedence is resolved at read time.

end_vote_threshold.description: RFC 0030 Layer 4 (v0.3.8) end-of-interaction quorum (K) for this channel: when K distinct participants emit an `END_INTERACTION_VOTE` action within `end_vote_window` consecutive turns, the interaction closes on its own and the orchestrator stops fanning out new replies (§H). Absent uses the K=2 default (one agent saying 'done' is not consensus; two distinct agents in close succession is); the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' — unlike `interaction_budget_tokens`, 0 is NOT a meaningful 'uncapped' value here — and rejects negatives at load time. Still opt-in: with no agent emitting the vote action, a populated K never fires, so existing channels are unchanged.

end_vote_window.description: RFC 0030 Layer 4 (v0.3.8) end-of-interaction recency window (W) for this channel: an end-vote counts toward the `end_vote_threshold` quorum only while it is within W consecutive turns of the current turn, so a stale vote from much earlier no longer counts ('votes must be recent'). A 'turn' is any tracked publish in the interaction (every message, not only votes), so in a busy channel the K distinct votes must land within W publishes of each other — tune W up if intervening chatter is starving the quorum. Absent uses the W=3 default (wide enough to survive an intervening one-off comment); the Go loader treats a zero/absent value as 'use the default' and rejects negatives at load time.

escalation_chair_id.description: The chair-stall-escalation amendment (RFC 0030 minimal Layer 5 slice, v0.3.8): the member who receives ONE forced turn after a stalled floor round (zero replies across ≥1 granted turns on the channel's open interaction) — prompted to synthesize and cast its end-of-discussion vote, or to call on the member best placed to continue. Must be one of this channel's declared members, not an `observer`, and the channel must not set `floor_control: false` (the loader rejects all three loudly — an observer's gate suppresses every turn, so it could never speak, and stall detection runs only at the floor round's tail, so without floor control the knob would be silently inert); it need not be declared `chair`. The pattern is the member `id` pattern, verbatim: the knob's domain is this channel's member ids. Closing still requires the Layer 4 vote quorum — the chair proposes, the quorum disposes. Absent (the default) disables escalation; deliberately distinct from the v0.4.0 moderator's `moderator_agent_id` (a non-participant trusted closer).

interaction_idle_timeout_seconds.description: This channel's interaction idle window in seconds (the RFC 0030 interaction-id producer, IP3): a publish arriving more than this long after the channel's last one retires the open interaction and mints a fresh one. Tri-state, unlike the integer knobs above: absent inherits `default_interaction_idle_timeout_seconds` (itself defaulting to 600), while an explicit 0 disables idle rotation for this channel — so no `default` is declared here (a schema default would erase the absent-vs-0 distinction the loader's pointer field preserves). Negative is rejected at load time.

reasoning.description: RFC 0051 (v0.3.10) reasoning-before-posting block. Before composing a reply an open-floor `participant`/`chair` privately decides WHETHER the turn is worth a post (`mode: bid`, the silence-only rung — the net pile-on saving) and, one rung up, WHAT the post should accomplish (`mode: plan`, threading a private composition plan into the compose). It generalizes the RFC 0030 Tier B scalar salience bid and RIDES that seam, so it is meaningful only on a channel with a salience-gated `participant`/`chair` member — the Go loader rejects `mode != off` on a channel without one (the knob does not by itself arm the gate). Ships dark in v0.3.10 (default `mode: off` = today's scalar score gate, under which the per-member `threshold` governs); the governed-channel default flips to `bid` in a later step. Absent fields normalize to the default rung (off / fast / shallow / 0).

mode.description: Deliberation rung. `off`: no deliberation — the byte-for-byte RFC 0030 Tier B scalar score gate (the per-member `threshold` governs here). `bid`: the persona privately decides `should_post` before the expensive compose, ending an unworthy turn in DO_NOTHING. `plan`: a `should_post=true` turn additionally threads a private CompositionPlan into the Tier C compose. The ladder is a strict superset chain `off ⊂ bid ⊂ plan`. The Go loader rejects a non-off mode on a channel with no salience-gated member.

model.description: Which leased model runs the deliberation pass. `fast` is the cheap model already in production for the Tier B bid (the default the net-saving economics assume). `quality` is accepted but warned at load — it defeats the cheap-pass economics (RFC 0051 §F).

depth.description: Deliberation depth. Only `shallow` is backed in v0.3.10; `deep` (native extended thinking) needs a provider-protocol change and is REJECTED at load by the Go capability gate until RFC 0051 Phase 4 (the enum lists it as the forward-compatible value space, but it is unbacked in this build — set it and the loader errors rather than silently degrading to shallow).

revise.description: Reflexion round count (RFC 0051 Phase 5). `0` is single-pass (the default). `>= 1` is REJECTED at load by the Go capability gate until the critic→revise loop is deployed (Phase 5); the schema permits the integer space, the loader is the deployment gate. Meaningful only under `mode: plan` (the critic checks the draft against the plan).

autonomous.description: RFC 0052 (v0.3.11) autonomous-discussion block — opt-in human-free convening. An armed channel (`enabled: true`) convenes a roster of personas on a topic and runs a discussion that converges, terminates, and synthesizes with no human in the loop. SAFETY: an armed channel cannot be created without an enforced per-interaction cost cap — the Go loader rejects `autonomous.enabled` unless the channel's resolved `interaction_budget_tokens` (per-channel, else `default_interaction_budget_tokens`) is positive — and its `convener` must be a declared member, not an observer (respond: never), and distinct from `escalation_chair_id` (the convener owns the agenda lifecycle, a separate role from the chair). Arming is group-only — the apply path rejects an `autonomous.enabled` DM/thread channel (convening is an open-floor group concept). LIVE as of v0.3.11 PR 3: an armed channel is convenable via `POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/convene`, which triggers real LLM spend with no human present — so arm deliberately. Ordinary channels omit the block and are byte-for-byte unchanged.

enabled.description: Arm the channel for human-free convening. Opt-in: false (the default) is an ordinary channel. The Go loader rejects an armed channel that has no enforced `interaction_budget_tokens` cap and one whose `convener` is empty, a non-member, an observer (respond: never), or equal to `escalation_chair_id`.

topic.description: Free-text subject the convener opens the discussion on. Wrapped as an RFC 0009 `<external_data>` envelope before injection (operator config is a distinct trust class from persona-authored content).

agenda.description: Optional ordered sub-topics the convener advances through on a stall (PR 6). Empty is a single-topic discussion. Bounded (max 64) because each item gets its own per-item escalation ration, so the agenda length bounds total convener turns.

convener.description: Agent id of the persona that authors the opening turn and advances the agenda. Must be one of this channel's declared members, must NOT be an `observer` (respond: never) — its receiver gate would suppress the opening turn before any LLM, exactly as for the escalation chair — and must be DISTINCT from `escalation_chair_id` (RFC 0052 OQ #1: the convener owns the agenda lifecycle; the chair keeps its shipped synthesis/close role). Same id vocabulary as `escalation_chair_id`.

goal.description: Free-text outcome the chair's goal-directed synthesis turn aims at on close (PR 4). Empty is a generic synthesis.

max_rounds.description: Hard floor-round bound — a second independent terminator alongside the cost cap. Absent/0 uses the 12 default; negative is rejected at load.

schedule_interval_seconds.description: RFC 0052 §E (v0.3.11) standing/scheduled convening — the RFC 0024 timer interval that re-convenes this channel. 0 (the default) is a one-shot channel (convened on demand); a positive value (>= 1s, the RFC 0024 busy-loop floor) makes the channel STANDING — the convener is re-woken every interval_seconds to open a fresh discussion. SAFETY: a standing channel re-opens a fresh, separately-capped interaction on every fire, so the per-interaction `interaction_budget_tokens` cap does NOT bound its recurring total — the Go loader rejects an armed standing channel that declares no aggregate bound (`max_convenings` and/or `standing_budget_tokens`), the §E mirror of the mandatory per-interaction cap. Ships DARK in PR 7a (parsed, validated, persisted, surfaced) — nothing fires the timer yet (the config-round-trip into the convener's agents.yaml timer set is a later PR).

max_convenings.description: RFC 0052 §E aggregate convening-count bound for a STANDING channel — the schedule stops re-convening after this many convenings. 0 (the default) is unset. A standing channel (positive `schedule_interval_seconds`) must declare this and/or `standing_budget_tokens`. Runtime enforcement is a later PR.

standing_budget_tokens.description: RFC 0052 §E aggregate standing-window cost budget for a STANDING channel — a ceiling on total spend across the recurring schedule, above the per-interaction `interaction_budget_tokens` cap that bounds each convening in isolation. 0 (the default) is unset. A standing channel (positive `schedule_interval_seconds`) must declare this and/or `max_convenings`. Runtime enforcement is a later PR.

members.description: Explicit, auditable membership list. The v0.2-era `members: "all"` shorthand was dropped per RFC 0011.

respond.description: Member disposition (RFC 0030 relevance amendment). Recommended vocabulary: `participant` (joins the open floor — speaks on un-addressed messages, subject to the Tier B salience bid), `chair` (a low-threshold facilitator: a `participant` that clears the salience bid readily and keeps the discussion moving — v0.3.8; it CANNOT close an interaction, convergence is owned by the governance layers, and its Layer 5 moderator hooks are reserved/inert until v0.4.0), `addressed` (speaks only when @-mentioned or replied to), `observer` (never speaks). The legacy values `always`/`when_mentioned`/`never` keep working and map to `participant`/`addressed`/`observer` respectively; the Go loader normalizes the disposition vocabulary back to the legacy three at load time (`chair` → `always` + a low default `threshold`), so the wire `respond_policy` and every downstream reader are unchanged.

threshold.description: Per-disposition salience threshold for the v0.3.8 Tier B relevance bid: an open-floor `participant` only reaches the (expensive) quality turn when its cheap salience bid clears this bar. Only meaningful on an open-floor disposition (`participant`/`chair`/legacy `always`); the Go loader rejects a `threshold` set on `addressed`/`observer`/`when_mentioned`, where no bid runs — a cross-field rule JSON Schema cannot express, so a schema-valid config can still fail to load. Bias-to-silence — an absent/unset threshold biases toward NOT replying on ambiguous open-floor traffic (the conservative default; calibration is post-soak). `chair` members get a low default so they speak readily. Bounded to the `[0, 1]` salience range (salience is clipped to `[0.0, 1.0]` per RFC 0024; mirrors `autonomy.salience_threshold` in agent.schema.json).

messageMetadata.description: Optional metadata bag on the publish payload (POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages → publishMessageRequest.metadata). Carries cross-cutting wire-level fields that are not part of the core message body. Documented here rather than in the channels.yaml config schema because the config file has no metadata of its own — this definition pins the REST publish contract, mirrored on the gRPC side by typed fields on ChannelMessageEvent.

cascade_depth.description: Hop count along the cooperative-path cascade chain (RFC 0011 amendment 'Cascade-depth wire propagation'). Documented operational range is [0, max_cascade_depth] (default cap 5). The schema enforces a lower bound only — values above the cap are accepted and clamped server-side at the orchestrator's publish boundary so a publisher does not need to know the deployment's current cap to compose a payload. Mirrors the typed `int32 cascade_depth = 11` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto).

interaction_id.description: RFC 0020 interaction_id of the open Interaction this message belongs to (RFC 0030 deterministic governance layers, v0.3.8). Opaque string token — RFC 0020 §D names it a ULID, but the agent-side implementation mints a uuid4 (agents/memory/interactions.py), so do not assume ULID sortability. Optional: absent is the untracked / pre-v0.3.8 case, which leaves every governance layer (Layer 1 cost ceiling, Layer 2 reply budget, Layer 4 end-of-interaction votes) at its uncapped default, so the field is additive. When a publisher supplies this key the orchestrator lifts it onto the typed `string interaction_id = 17` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto) so the value survives the publish→fanout boundary that has no metadata map. Bounded at 128 (mirrors the agent receive path's thread_id cap, generous over the 36-char uuid4) — the layer PRs key per-interaction maps on this value, so an over-length claim is treated as untracked (the value dropped) rather than riding an unbounded map key through. This schema is the documentary expression of that bound (`maxLength` counts code units); the runtime enforcement counts UTF-8 bytes and lives at BOTH boundaries that touch the value — the orchestrator publish boundary (`readInteractionID`, internal/channels/interaction_id.go) and the agent receive seed (`seed_wire_metadata`, agents/channel_wire_metadata.py), each degrading to untracked rather than failing the dispatch. The producer is live since v0.3.8 (the interaction-id producer plan): the orchestrator's own resolver stamps the key on every routed publish (`publishCommit`, internal/channels/router_publish_async.go), REPLACING any inbound claim — a publisher-supplied value is read only for the divergence debug log and never keys governance state.

end_interaction_vote.description: RFC 0030 Layer 4 (v0.3.8) end-of-interaction vote flag: when an agent emits an `END_INTERACTION_VOTE` action, the publish that carries it sets this to `true` so the orchestrator counts it toward the channel's `end_vote_threshold` quorum (scoped by `interaction_id`; a vote with no `interaction_id` is ignored). Absent/false is an ordinary message. The orchestrator reads it at the publish boundary (`readEndInteractionVote`, internal/channels/end_vote.go) and, once K distinct participants have voted within `end_vote_window` consecutive turns, closes the interaction and suppresses further fanout. The producer is live since v0.3.8: the Python vote producer (`publish_end_interaction_vote`, agents/end_vote_action.py) merges the flag into every published vote's metadata.

previous_interaction_id.description: RFC 0030 producer plan OQ 5 (v0.3.8): the channel's most recently RETIRED interaction id, stamped by the orchestrator (`publishCommit`, internal/channels/router_publish_async.go) onto every publish of the SUCCESSOR interaction together with `previous_interaction_close_trigger` — the close-cause attribution the agent-side rotation close uses to label the local boundary truthfully. Router-authoritative like `interaction_id`: an inbound claim under this key is STRIPPED on commit (a publisher can never forge a close cause), so on read surfaces the value is always the resolver's own record. Absent is the no-retiree case (fresh channel, post-restart re-mint, pre-v0.3.8 rows) and receivers keep the legacy structural label. Same 128-byte bound and enforcement posture as `interaction_id`; the pair is validated as a unit at both the dispatcher lift (`readPreviousClose`, internal/channels/interaction_id.go) and the agent receive seed (`seed_wire_metadata`, agents/channel_wire_metadata.py) — mirrored on the gRPC side by the typed `string previous_interaction_id = 20` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto).

previous_interaction_close_trigger.description: The trigger that retired `previous_interaction_id` — `idle` (lazy idle rotation) or `end_votes` (Layer 4 quorum close), the §L instrument vocabulary. Set iff `previous_interaction_id` is set (the pair travels and validates as a unit; a lone trigger attributes nothing). Stamped and stripped exactly like its sibling; the agent-side rotation close maps `idle` → the `idle_gap` close reason and everything else (including absent) → the legacy `structural` label, so an unrecognised value degrades rather than failing the dispatch. Mirrors the typed `string previous_interaction_close_trigger = 21` field on `ChannelMessageEvent` (proto/task.proto).

publishMessageRequest.description: RFC 0040 Phase 1 (v0.3.14): the request body of POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages — the agent→orchestrator channel-publish contract, pinned over today's REST path BEFORE the dual-surface window opens (RFC 0040 Motivation 1, drift risk). Mirrors `publishMessageRequest` (internal/server/channel_types.go) field-for-field; the Python producer is `HttpChannelPublisher.publish` (agents/channel_publisher.py). Phase 2 adds a SEPARATE protobuf contract for the agent→orchestrator hop — it does not retire this schema, because the REST publish endpoint is never removed (it is the client edge, RFC 0040 §Migration). `additionalProperties: false` is deliberate and is the drift trip-wire: a field added to the Go struct without a matching entry here fails the cross-language pin (tests/unit/python/test_channel_payload_contract.py) rather than reaching the wire unreviewed.

sender_id.description: REQUIRED publishing identity. The orchestrator does not infer sender identity over REST — the agent-side ActionExecutor populates it from its registered ID, and human clients (CLI, curl) supply it explicitly. Non-empty: an empty sender is rejected at the handler, so the schema pins the same floor rather than letting a blank value round-trip. NOT the RFC 0040 §D `sender_id` scope question (that bears on the Phase 2 proto and is an Open Question against the Accepted flip) — this entry only records today's REST behaviour.

content.description: REQUIRED message body, non-empty. `handlePublishMessage` (internal/server/channel_handlers.go) rejects an empty `content` with a 400 `BAD_REQUEST` on the line after the identical `sender_id` check, so the schema pins the same floor on both — a contract that accepted `""` would stay silent on the publish shape most likely to be rejected on the wire. Note the agent-side reachability: `ActionExecutor` reads the body as `action.payload.get("content", "")` with no emptiness guard, so a model that omits the key produces exactly this payload; the send-side WARN is what names it before the 400 does.

thread_id.description: Optional parent-message anchor. Present makes the publish a threaded reply; absent is a channel-level post. Threads are implicit (never declared in channels.yaml), so this is the only place the anchor travels.

mentions.description: Optional explicit @-mention list, consumed by the `addressed` respond-policy path. Omitted entirely when empty — the Python producer only sets the key on a truthy list, so `"mentions": []` is not a shape this producer emits.

channel_type.description: Optional cross-check against the channel's derived `<channel_type>:<name>` address (RFC 0011 §C). Advisory: the orchestrator resolves the channel from the path segment and uses this only to detect a caller-side mismatch.

metadata.description: Optional cross-cutting wire fields. Note the producer's shape rule (agents/channel_publisher.py): the key is omitted entirely unless the bag is non-empty, so a routine publish carries no `"metadata": {}`. Router-authoritative keys inside it (`interaction_id`, `previous_interaction_id`, `previous_interaction_close_trigger`) are stamped or stripped on commit regardless of what a publisher claims.

session_id.description: Optional RFC 0031 Phase 3 `--session` override: replaces the orchestrator's boot-default session for this one publish, both as the persisted row's `session_id` and as the emitted `persatrix-session` header. Absent leaves the boot default / ISSUE-0082 auto-binding standing. NOT in the RFC 0040 Phase 1 field list (which predates it) — see the schema's own drift note: the RFC enumerated four fields in 2026-07 and two identity-axis fields have landed since.

epoch_id.description: Optional ISSUE-0085 PR 5 `--epoch` override: replaces the boot-resolved process epoch as the emitted `persatrix-epoch` header (the run/test-isolation axis, orthogonal to `session_id`'s room-continuity axis). Unlike `session_id` it is NOT stamped on the persisted row. Absent leaves the boot epoch standing.

channelMessage.description: RFC 0040 Phase 1 (v0.3.14): one message as returned by the publish, history, and thread endpoints. Mirrors `channelMessageResponse` (internal/server/channel_types.go). The Python consumer is `HttpChannelHistoryFetcher.fetch` (agents/channel_history_fetcher.py), which returns the raw `messages` list to the on-startup catch-up replay and the RFC 0034 conversation window.

channel_id.description: Canonical channel address the message belongs to.

sender_id.description: Publishing identity, echoed from the publish request.

timestamp.description: Server-assigned instant, RFC 3339 (Go `time.Time` marshalling — date, `T`, time, optional fractional seconds, then `Z` or a numeric offset). Always present — the field carries no `omitempty`, and the zero time would serialise rather than vanish. `pattern`, not `format`, is what actually bites: draft-07 `format` is an annotation unless the validator is handed a `format_checker`, and even then jsonschema's `date-time` check is a no-op unless the optional `rfc3339-validator` package is installed — which the agent image does not ship. Enforcing the shape through a dependency that may silently be absent would rebuild the inert pin this replaces, so the regex carries the assertion and `format` is kept for its documentation/codegen value only.

thread_id.description: Parent-message anchor for a threaded reply; omitted on a channel-level message.

mentions.description: Explicit @-mention list. REQUIRED and never `null`: the field carries no `omitempty`, so a nil Go slice would marshal as `null` — the response builder therefore normalises nil to `[]` (internal/server/channel_response_builders.go). That normalisation is load-bearing for every client that iterates the list without a null guard; this entry is what fails if it is removed.

metadata.description: Cross-cutting wire fields persisted with the message; omitted when empty.

principal_id.description: ISSUE-0130 shape (b) (v0.3.15, channel store v12): the tenant the orchestrator attributed this publish to — the RFC 0039 §F verified participant of the authenticated request, or `local` when no account resolved (every unauthenticated caller, the whole persona fleet, and every request under `auth.mode: disabled`). Stamped SERVER-SIDE at publish and never read from the request body: `publishMessageRequest` has no counterpart and the handler rejects unknown keys, because an agent-supplied principal would be a cross-tenant read primitive once catch-up replay seeds a `principal_scope` from this field. REQUIRED and never omitted — the consumer is a seed, and an absent key is indistinguishable from a pre-v12 orchestrator, which is the one ambiguity the replay attribution has to resolve; `local` is a real answer, not a missing one.

channelHistoryResponse.description: RFC 0040 Phase 1 (v0.3.14): the envelope returned by GET /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages and the thread endpoint. Mirrors `historyResponse` (internal/server/channel_types.go). Consumed by `HttpChannelHistoryFetcher.fetch`, whose contract degrades a non-object body or an unusable `messages` field to `[]` rather than raising — so a schema violation here is a silently-empty window, exactly the failure mode this pin exists to catch.

messages.description: Ordered message list, oldest first. Present even when empty.

classification.description: RFC 0037 §A channel-level confidentiality — one value per envelope, never per message (a message's classification IS its channel's, §H). Carries no `omitempty`, so the key is always present; the empty string is an accepted value and resolves to the `public` acting floor receiver-side (§A rule (b)), which is why `""` is in the enum rather than being rejected as a malformed level.
